title: Subgingival Microbiome in Children with Gingival Inflammation and Healthy Subjects
content: (1) Background: The aim of this study is to investigate and compare key microorganisms of the subgingival microflora in healthy children and children with diagnosed gingival inflammation (ages 10-14). (2) Methods: Each child underwent a clinical periodontal examination at four levels: General Health Status Assessment, Oral Hygiene Status Assessment by HI index, Assessment of Teeth and Gingiva, Gingival Sulcus Assessment by PBI index. PCR-Real Time Method for Identifying Subgingival Microorganisms was used. (3) Results: 73 children aged 10 to 14 years underwent clinical periodontal examination. Four of the examined periodontopathogens (A. actinomycetemcomitans, P. gingivalis, T. denticola, and E. nodatum) were not isolated in healthy children. In the group of children with gingival inflammation, the frequency of isolation of T. forsythia was significantly higher (p < 0.05). In children with gingival inflammation, the highest quantities of isolated periodontopathogens were P. intermedia and C. gingivalis. The representatives microorganisms of the purple and yellow complexes are found only in children with gingival inflammation. (4) Conclusion: The highly pathogenic representatives of the red complex according to Socransky are detected in all children with gingival inflammation.
